title: Neo4j Practice
description: Practise the twelve ideas in this Neo4j course. Choose an answer, then read why it fits the example.

exercises.question: What is Book in this pattern?
options: A node label
A relationship direction
exercises.explanation: A node represents one thing. A label says what kind of thing it is, and properties hold its named facts.

exercises.question: Which clause finds existing graph patterns?
options: CREATE every time
MATCH
exercises.explanation: MATCH finds graph patterns. A property condition can choose the node with a known id.

exercises.question: What does this constraint make unique?
options: Book.id values
Every word in every title
exercises.explanation: A uniqueness constraint prevents two nodes with a label from sharing the same chosen property value.

exercises.question: Why merge on id and then set title?
options: SET creates a new label every time
The id is stable while the title may change
exercises.explanation: MERGE finds a pattern or creates it if missing. Merge on a stable key, then SET fields that may change.

exercises.question: What does (r)-[:READ]->(b) mean?
options: The reader has a READ relationship to the book
The book is a text field inside the reader
exercises.explanation: A relationship gives two nodes a named connection and direction. Its type explains what that connection means.

exercises.question: What information is being followed?
options: The row order in a table
The READ connections from the reader
exercises.explanation: A pattern can follow a known relationship to related nodes. This is how a graph answers connection questions.

exercises.question: Which book passes the 50-page rule?
options: Moon Trip with 60 pages
Garden Days with 40 pages
exercises.explanation: WHERE adds a condition to a matched pattern. It can filter a numeric property such as page count.

exercises.question: Why add ORDER BY before LIMIT?
options: To add a new relationship
To define which result is first
exercises.explanation: ORDER BY sorts returned rows from a graph query. LIMIT keeps only the chosen number.

exercises.question: What does count(DISTINCT b) avoid?
options: Counting the same matched book more than once
Reading every book property at all
exercises.explanation: An aggregate can summarise matched relationships. COUNT counts the matched book values in each group.

exercises.question: What does OPTIONAL MATCH preserve?
options: Only rows that have every possible relationship
The earlier row even without a matching optional relationship
exercises.explanation: OPTIONAL MATCH keeps the earlier row even when the optional connection is missing. Missing values appear as null.

exercises.question: Where is finishedOn stored here?
options: On the READ relationship
On every Book node
exercises.explanation: Relationships can hold properties too. A property can describe the connection itself, such as when a reader finished a book.

exercises.question: Why inspect the MATCH before deletion?
options: To make deletion reversible automatically
To confirm the exact node and connections being removed
exercises.explanation: A connected node cannot be deleted normally while its relationships remain. DETACH DELETE removes that node and its attached relationships.
